author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Science Cafe is returning to Concord for a one-night public discussion focused on artificial intelligence. The free event is scheduled for Tuesday, September 15, from 6 to 8 p.m. at Litherman’s Limited brewery, 126 Hall Street, the Concord Monitor reported.

The format places expert panelists at a table to answer questions from attendees instead of presenting a formal lecture. Organizers expect the conversation to examine how AI works, where it falls short and how it could affect work, education and daily life. Food and beverages will be available, and organizers advised arriving early because of strong interest.

The panelists are Nicholas Smith, a University of New Hampshire philosophy professor, and James Dobson, a Dartmouth College English professor and writing-program director. Smith has worked with a UNH summer program on governing AI, while Dobson has served as a special adviser to Dartmouth’s provost on the technology.

Science Cafe held recurring sessions in Concord before the pandemic. This gathering is not a restart of the old monthly schedule, though organizers said future one-off events remain possible. Similar public science conversations continue in Nashua and Manchester.
dek: The free September 15 session will bring UNH and Dartmouth humanities scholars to Litherman’s Limited for questions about artificial intelligence.
headline: Concord Science Cafe returns with public conversation about AI
